meta.premiseEvidence: Direct route, component, contract, security, build, Lighthouse, browser, leaderboard, control-plane, status, and current-project documentation inspection. Production Lighthouse evidence measured median LCP 3.226s for the default route versus 2.651s for HomeV1. Browser E2E was 7/8 in the concurrent suite and the failed pointer case passed alone, so readiness is flaky rather than green. The live leaderboard audit found one implausible historical row. No retention, balance, physical-device, delivery, funnel, or new subjective-pixel claim is inferred.

baseline.release: FORGE and NO-GO for launch promotion; isolated implementation and staging work may continue.
baseline.performance: Default production median LCP 3.226s, TBT 115ms, performance 0.88; HomeV1 LCP 2.651s. Main bundle 730,334 raw bytes and data chunk 220,404 raw bytes.
baseline.architecture: src/App.jsx is 4,999/5,000 lines. main.jsx eagerly imports App and idle-scheduled leaderboard work can pull network/data into the LCP window.
baseline.quality: Session evidence reports 935/935 automated tests; current browser run was 7/8 with the lone pointer test passing in isolation.
baseline.trust: Release security audit 8/8, npm audit zero, replay trust 3/3; live leaderboard audit exposed one implausible public row and its audit script bypasses the secrets gateway.
baseline.identity: There is no real logged-in user panel or cloud progress sync. Login copy promises carried progress while callback stores an identity receipt locally and returns home.
baseline.intelligence: Run coaching is deterministic and local, with zero hosted-model/API token consumption; intelligence is deep but fragmented across overlapping surfaces.
baseline.content: Seventeen public routes are structurally registered, but twelve share a generic card-grid shell, changelog freshness stops July 25, LIVE_OPS calls the app frontend-only despite five edge functions, and status lacks timestamped machine-readable truth.
baseline.visualEvidence: Existing hash-bound receipt reports 867/867 objective checks across 17 routes, two themes, and three widths. Fresh subjective all-page visual inspection could not be completed because the Windows image/browser host repeatedly failed CryptUnprotectData; no new aesthetic pass is claimed.

gameLoopReview.evidence: The escalation loop, twelve-weapon improvisation, deterministic contracts, humiliation-to-revenge voice, coaching, rivalry, ghosts, and replay systems form an unusually coherent foundation. The main weakness is not missing systems but overlapping explanation and action surfaces after a run and on the front door. No receipt-backed participant corpus exists, so fun, pacing, balance, or retention outcomes remain hypotheses.

items.title: Restore a trustworthy startup and release evidence plane before feature work.
items.verification: startup:acceptance PASS; protocol:drift 37/37; 40/40 focused control-plane tests. The CANON-045 boolean passIf parser defect was routed to its studio-ops owner through signed Ark cargo rather than mutated cross-repo.
items.why: startup:acceptance currently crashes in startup-acceptance.mjs, protocol drift is 36/37 because capability-map verification fails, the generated startup brief misses required sections, and canon conformance cannot parse CANON-045. A broken evidence plane can falsely certify or block every later wave.
items.recipe: Repair the acceptance formatter and capability-map isolated-checkout fixture, make the brief renderer consume canonical sections, and fix the CANON-045 parser. Add one bounded acceptance command that proves startup brief schema, secrets provenance without values, canon parseability, protocol drift, and public-repo artifact policy. Emit a hash-bound receipt and require it before release evidence is trusted.

L1.recipe: Stop the acceptance crash and restore truthful nonzero capability evidence.

L2.recipe: Fix brief and CANON-045 parsing with regression fixtures at the real entry points.

L3.recipe: Create one hash-bound evidence-plane court covering startup, drift, canon, secrets provenance, and public boundaries.

items.title: Build a two-phase boot boundary that protects first paint from the game runtime and data plane.
items.verification: Entry JavaScript fell from about 734KB to 196KB raw; runtime/request boundary tests pass; isolated staging three-run median is performance 1.00, LCP 1.301s, CLS 0, TBT 8ms.
items.why: The default production route is 575ms slower in LCP than HomeV1, the main bundle is 730KB raw, App.jsx sits at 4,999/5,000 lines, and idle-scheduled leaderboard work can still execute before LCP. The front door pays for runtime and data it does not need to show its first useful frame.
items.recipe: Split a lightweight shell/router from the arena runtime, lazy-import App only on play intent or a safe post-LCP boundary, move leaderboard/Supabase refresh behind visibility plus consented intent, and prefetch the arena on hover/focus/idle only after the hero settles. Extract one runtime facade instead of scattering imports. Add bundle budgets, request chronology assertions, three-run production medians, and rollback if interaction readiness regresses.

L1.recipe: Defer leaderboard/data work until after LCP and visible intent.

L2.recipe: Lazy-load the arena runtime behind a small front-door shell with intent prefetch.

L3.recipe: Ship a versioned runtime facade, bundle/request budgets, production median receipt, and accessibility-safe loading state.

items.title: Turn the fragmented coach stack into one local Insight Graph and one decisive debrief.
items.verification: Versioned deterministic evidence nodes, causal deduplication, contradiction penalties, one Verdict/Lesson/Action, expandable evidence, agent projection, and focused fixtures pass with zero hosted-model tokens.
items.why: DeathScreen exposes many individually strong but overlapping coach, fairness, performance, Run the Fix, intelligence, collapse, rivalry, proof, replay, and share cards. Players must interpret the system instead of receiving one trusted answer. Hosted-model cost is already zero and should stay zero.
items.recipe: Define typed local evidence nodes for observation, cause, confidence, contradiction, lesson, and action. Adapt existing runCoach/runBrain/runIntelligence outputs into the graph, deduplicate by causal fingerprint, penalize contradictions, and render one Verdict plus optional Why drawer and one executable next-run action. Keep deterministic fixtures, agent-readable JSON, explainability, and a stable version field; do not add a hosted large language model.

L1.recipe: Rank existing insights and show only one primary lesson/action.

L2.recipe: Normalize all coach inputs into typed evidence with deduplication and confidence.

L3.recipe: Ship the versioned Insight Graph, contradiction handling, human debrief, agent projection, and exhaustive causal fixtures.

items.title: Promote the hidden flight recorder into a privacy-safe Playtest Pulse.
items.verification: Explicit persistent opt-in, bounded local aggregate, flight IDs, clarity/replay metrics, clear/export controls, and unit coverage ship; upload and balance changes remain gated until a consented corpus exists.
items.why: The app already has a local playtest recorder and two useful questions, but it is hidden behind a query parameter and has no corpus. Numerical tuning and retention claims therefore lack human evidence even though the collection primitive exists.
items.recipe: Expose an opt-in post-run Pulse at sampled cadence, capture structured friction events and two low-burden answers locally, show exactly what will be shared, and export a redacted diagnostic bundle. Add offline aggregation and a maintainer analysis command. Only at L3 add capped, consented upload through the existing data plane with abuse controls, deletion policy, and cost alarms.

L1.recipe: Expose local opt-in Pulse and redacted export.

L2.recipe: Add sampled prompts, offline aggregation, friction taxonomy, and evidence dashboard.

L3.recipe: Add capped consented upload, retention controls, deletion path, and cost/abuse receipts.

items.title: Quarantine implausible scores and make public score APIs fail safely under abuse.
items.verification: Live migration and both edge functions deployed; origin allowlist, quotas, replay controls, secrets-gateway audit, reversible quarantine receipt, 5/5 health, 3/3 replay smoke, and 36-row live audit with zero remaining flags.
items.why: A live audit found a public score over one million with implausible progression. The audit reports but exits successfully, reads .env.local directly, and does not quarantine. Edge functions allow wildcard origins and public token/submit endpoints consume finite invocation quota.
items.recipe: Route the audit through the secrets gateway, assign reason-coded severity, make actionable anomalies fail CI/release checks, quarantine rather than delete historical rows, and add an operator review/restore receipt. Restrict origins to declared production/staging origins, add per-IP and per-receipt limits, replay-resistant issuance budgets, and risk-triggered Turnstile only after suspicious thresholds. Preserve guest play and measure false positives.

L1.recipe: Use the secrets gateway, fail on high-confidence anomalies, and hide the known row pending review.

L2.recipe: Add quarantine/restore receipts, origin allowlists, and bounded rate limits.

L3.recipe: Ship adaptive abuse scoring, risk-triggered challenge, cost alarms, and adversarial trust fixtures.

items.title: Make the Obelisk login a truthful optional Porcelain Passport instead of a phantom account panel.
items.verification: Optional local receipt/export/import Passport, truthful login/callback copy, privacy and terms updates, auth route contracts, both themes, and focused fixtures ship; cloud sync is not claimed.
items.why: Login promises progress carried across games, but callback only stores a local identity receipt and returns home. Login/callback are absent from the public route and visual QA registry, privacy/terms omit receipt handling, and there is no logged-in panel or cloud sync.
items.recipe: Immediately rewrite copy to describe local identity verification, add login/callback to route, accessibility, theme, and visual QA contracts, minimize and version stored receipt fields, and document retention/removal. Add a small Passport panel showing verification state and local export/import backup. Treat Obelisk cross-device progress sync as an explicit gated L3 integration; guest play remains first class.

L1.recipe: Correct promises and cover login/callback in privacy, routing, accessibility, themes, and QA.

L2.recipe: Add a minimal Passport panel plus integrity-checked local export/import.

L3.recipe: Integrate Obelisk cross-device sync only after architecture, consent, recovery, and deletion gates pass.

items.axis: front door / information architecture / visual craft
items.title: Recompose HomeV2 as an elite porcelain operations table with one decision per region.
items.verification: Orders, Operations, Player Progress, Field Manual, and Support replace overlapping navigation/actions; one settings launcher remains. Hosted 19-route, two-theme, three-width pixel court passes 969/969.
items.why: Home duplicates recommendations, quick actions, settings, career/progression, support, and informational entry points. The density advertises breadth but weakens hierarchy and makes the next valuable action harder to recognize.
items.recipe: Create four deliberate zones: Hero/Deploy, Orders, Player Progress, and Field Manual/Help. Feed Orders from one continuation contract; collapse career/stats/meta/upgrades/missions/mastery into one hub; retain one settings launcher; make secondary content contextual drawers. Establish a distinctive porcelain/tactical-diagram art direction with restrained motion and clear depth. Capture desktop/mobile, both themes, every touched drawer, keyboard/controller focus, and reduced-motion states in a new hash-bound visual receipt.

L1.recipe: Remove duplicated launchers and establish one visual/action hierarchy.

L2.recipe: Build the four-zone responsive composition and unified Progress hub.

L3.recipe: Deliver elite art direction, motion grammar, full state/theme parity, and subjective plus objective visual QA.

items.axis: public website / content truth / dual audience
items.title: Replace templated public pages with a versioned Field Manual projected for humans and agents.
items.verification: Effective-dated source-bound claim cards now project to human UI, field-manual.json, status.json, agents.json, llms.txt, and gameplay contracts; public contract court passes 27/27.
items.why: Twelve routes repeat the same hero/card grid, Keep Exploring block, and flat 17-link footer. Public changelog and operations copy are stale, status is generic, and the in-game Codex can drift from public guides.
items.recipe: Define one versioned content graph with claims, audience, source, effective date, and route projections. Give routes purpose-built layouts: weapon bench, threat atlas, mode matrix, observed-action tutorial, transparent status timeline, and grouped navigation. Generate agents.json, llms.txt, JSON-LD, status.json, in-game Codex, sitemap, changelog, and route freshness tests from compatible source nodes. Preserve all canonical URLs and add contextual related links instead of flattening everything.

L1.recipe: Correct changelog, live-ops, identity, status, and contact truth; group navigation.

L2.recipe: Build the versioned content graph and source-derived human/agent projections.

L3.recipe: Ship route-specific interactive Field Manual layouts, freshness courts, structured data, and full visual QA.

items.title: Create shareable Scenario Cartridges and an asynchronous Sewer Relay without realtime infrastructure.
items.verification: Versioned bounded schema, sanitizer, checksum, base64url import/export, URL relay, browser editor, agent contract, and fixtures ship. Cryptographic signatures, inherited ghost batons, moderation, and rotation remain later gates.
items.why: The game already has deterministic seeds, modes, loadouts, ghosts, challenge links, and proof receipts, but they are separate primitives. A compact scenario grammar can create near-infinite authored and agent-authored challenges at negligible runtime cost.
items.recipe: Define a signed/versioned cartridge containing seed, mode, difficulty, loadout, mutations, route/objective, expiry, and proof policy. Encode it in a bounded URL or import file with schema and abuse limits. Build Sewer Relay as asynchronous baton play: one player completes a leg, the next inherits a verified ghost and modified objective. Expose a constrained agent creation schema with validation, simulation preview, accessibility metadata, and no arbitrary text/code execution.

L1.recipe: Create a cartridge schema, validator, importer, and deterministic single-player challenge.

L2.recipe: Add sharing, proof receipts, mutations, browser editor, and agent-readable authoring contract.

L3.recipe: Ship asynchronous Sewer Relay, inherited ghosts, moderation/expiry, and cost-bounded community rotation.

items.title: Restore document zoom and confine gesture suppression to the active arena.
items.verification: Global scaling restrictions were removed, gesture suppression is arena-scoped, and public/auth/home routes pass responsive geometry and contrast at 390px, 768px, and 1440px.
items.why: The document viewport disables user scaling globally, penalizing low-vision visitors across marketing, legal, help, login, and status pages even though gesture control is only needed during active play.
items.recipe: Remove maximum-scale and user-scalable=no from the document viewport. Apply touch-action, overscroll, selection, and gesture prevention only to the mounted arena surface and only while play is active. Verify 200%/400% zoom, reflow, dialogs, navigation, legal pages, login, pointer lock, touch aiming, and controller prompts on desktop and mobile.

L2.recipe: Scope all gesture suppression to the active arena.

L3.recipe: Add zoom/reflow/touch regression coverage across public, auth, menu, modal, and game states.

items.title: Turn repeated enemies and failures into a personal Nemesis Chronicle with three-run revenge arcs.
items.verification: Existing career/grudge evidence now produces a local three-chapter dossier, targeted counter-move, cosmetic border signal, agent projection, and deterministic fixtures without adding a power currency.
items.why: Grudges, repeat killers, rivalry, run narrative, and coaching already identify emotionally charged opponents, but they do not compound into a durable authored arc. The missing layer is memory and payoff, not another currency.
items.recipe: Promote evidence-backed repeat killers or failure patterns into opt-in three-run arcs: insult, adaptation, showdown. Track only local cosmetic narrative state, explain promotion criteria, and let the Insight Graph generate a targeted practice/rematch action. Reward closure with titles, porcelain cracks, dossier stamps, or Chronicle pages, not power. Cap recurrence, allow dismissal/reset, and verify it never misstates causality or blocks ordinary play.

L1.recipe: Create a local dossier from existing grudge and run narrative signals.

L2.recipe: Add deterministic three-run arcs, targeted rematches, and cosmetic closure.

L3.recipe: Integrate Chronicle art, accessible narrative modes, agent-readable state, tuning limits, and long-horizon playtest evidence.

items.title: Generate a small hot context layer and archive historical operational prose without losing evidence.
items.verification: Deterministic HOT_CONTEXT.json/md projections remain below 24KB, include source SHA-256/byte provenance, and pass freshness/check fixtures. Authoritative histories remain intact; no destructive archive migration was performed.
items.why: CURRENT_STATE, TASK_BOARD, and DECISIONS total more than 300KB, while public docs and generated receipts duplicate truth. Large indiscriminate reads increase agent tokens and make stale statements easier to repeat. Runtime AI token cost is already zero.
items.recipe: Define source ownership for current status, decisions, tasks, public facts, and evidence. Generate a bounded HOT_CONTEXT.json/md containing only current objective, release posture, top open work, invariants, and pointers. Move completed history into indexed immutable archives, add section/range query helpers, deduplicate generated prose, and enforce byte/staleness budgets in startup. Preserve signed hashes and git history; never summarize away legal, security, or decision records.

L1.recipe: Generate a bounded hot-context projection with authoritative pointers.

L2.recipe: Archive completed history, add indexed retrieval, and remove duplicative generated prose.

L3.recipe: Enforce context byte/freshness budgets, signed archive indexes, and task-aware minimal loading fixtures.

skipped.reason: No participant corpus supports changing weapon, enemy, wave, or economy numbers yet; instrument first.
The local deterministic intelligence stack is strong and costs zero tokens; a hosted model adds latency, privacy, reliability, and spend without a verified quality gap.
Existing event proof, ghosts, GIFs, and Run Story composition provide higher leverage at lower storage and privacy cost.
Guest play is a core strength; identity must remain optional and honest.
Asynchronous cartridges and relays reuse deterministic primitives without realtime infrastructure cost or moderation burden.
Default HomeV2 is currently slower and funnel evidence is absent; the existing retirement gate has not passed.
The canonical routes serve distinct intents; consolidate their source graph and navigation rather than break URLs.
The project has sufficient content breadth; comprehension, evidence, and compounding systems have higher leverage.
All promoted work can begin with existing internal tools and dependencies; package trust should gate any later exception.
Exact-current staging, empirical play evidence, trust cleanup, physical-device proof, contact identity, and founder approval remain open.

research.title: web.dev Optimize LCP
research.use: A good LCP target is 2.5 seconds or less and JavaScript-delayed discovery/execution can harm LCP.

research.title: Cloudflare rate limiting
research.use: Bound public abuse at the edge without making every legitimate player solve a challenge.
